newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 3.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet approved a plan for rents to increase most in big cities beginning in the summer of this year. In Prague, regulated rents will, at most, double, and in areas with more than 100,000 residents, rents could increase by up to 62 percent. In the entire country, rents will increase by approximately 50 percent.
- Komercni Banka closed its accounts with gross profits of 5.492 billion crowns last year, which means profits after taxes of 5.36 billion, according to the bank's spokeswoman Irena Satavova.
- The power company CEZ expects a decrease in net profits for 1997 to 6.1 billion crowns and an increase in sales and revenue to 64.2 billion crowns, which is 3.2 billion crowns more than last year.
- According to Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, the cabinet coalition reached an agreement for increasing value added tax for electricity and natural gas to 22 percent from July 1 of this year.
PRAVO - Workers at Poldi Steel still did not receive their wages for December and January on Friday and continue to strike.

- Skoda Ostrov, a subsidiary of Skoda Plzen, exported the first four trolleybuses to the city of Dayton, Ohio. According to a spokesman for Skoda, a total of 54 trolleybuses worth more than $30 million should be supplied to the United States.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Social Democratic Party could be changing its campaign programme on a few issues. If during their convention, which begins in two weeks, they approve the changes, it will mean, among other things, that they will agree with the coalition on deregulation of energy prices and rents.

- The chairman of the parliamentary defence committee, Petr Necas, insists that crisis plans, according to which state institutions and administrations should operate in case of a catastrophe or if the country is in danger, are just as important as the condition of the army for entry into NATO.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The cabinet will meet on Wednesday to decide whether the director of Czech Railways, Rudolf Mladek, will lose his job. The railway workers union is waiting for the cabinet's decision to see if another strike is necessary, according to Jaromir Dusek, the union's chairman.

- The Film "Kolja" became the most successful Czech film of 1996. Its director, Jan Sverak, screenplay writer, Zdenek Sverak and six-year-old Andrej Chalimon in the title role all won Czech Lions for their parts.
